text: あ、これは早くも見事な一品との出会いが
translation: Oh my — what a magnificent find, and so early on!

vocabulary.meaning: a single item; an article (of quality)

grammar: The sentence ends mid-phrase with が, leaving the predicate implied — a common device for expressing excited, trailing-off speech.

text: これが噴水、命の源たる水をもてあそぶ
translation: So this is a fountain — toying with water, the very source of life…

vocabulary.meaning: to toy with; to play with recklessly

grammar: 〜たる is a classical/literary attributive form of だ (equivalent to modern 〜である), adding a formal, elevated tone: 命の源たる水 = 'water that is the source of life.'

text: 罪深きアート
translation: …a sinfully beautiful work of art.
grammar: 罪深き is the classical/literary attributive (連体形) of 罪深い, giving an archaic, elevated register appropriate to Elizabeth's speech.

text: その魔性ゆえに効果を投げ入れたものの願いを
translation: And because of its bewitching power, could it even grant the wishes of those who toss coins into it…

vocabulary.meaning: coin (here likely a mishearing/transcription of 硬貨; coin)
to throw into; to toss in

grammar: 〜ゆえに is a formal/literary causal conjunction meaning 'because of; on account of,' more elevated than から or ので.

text: 叶えてしまうものまであるのか
translation: …to the point of actually making them come true?

vocabulary.meaning: to grant; to make (a wish) come true
completion/finality; going so far as to (do something)

grammar: 〜てしまうものまであるのか combines 〜てしまう (completed/extreme action) with まである ('there are even those that…'), expressing surprised wonder.

text: いいえ私この時のためにと意気込んで
translation: No, no — I had actually worked myself up for this very moment and…

vocabulary.meaning: to be enthusiastic; to psych oneself up
for this purpose; for this occasion

grammar: The sentence ends with the te-form 意気込んで, trailing off to set up the next utterance — a common narrative device creating suspense or continuation.

text: 効果を少々持ってまいりました
translation: I brought along a small number of coins.

vocabulary.meaning: brought (humble form of 持ってきました)

grammar: まいる (参る) is the humble equivalent of 来る/行く; 持ってまいりました is the humble-past of 'brought with me,' reflecting Elizabeth's extremely polite register.

text: 500円効果に数えまして2000枚
translation: Counting them at 500 yen apiece — that comes to 2,000 coins.

vocabulary.meaning: coin (likely intended reading behind transcribed 効果)
flat object counter (for coins, sheets, etc.)

grammar: 〜にて is a formal/classical instrumental particle (equivalent to で), used here as 500円にて = 'reckoning at 500 yen each,' adding to Elizabeth's archaic register.

text: 締めて100万円からスタートでございます
translation: In total, we shall begin with one million yen.

vocabulary.meaning: in total; altogether (summing up a figure)

grammar: でございます is the highly polite/formal copula (丁寧語), a hallmark of Elizabeth's speech throughout; it is the polite equivalent of です, used in formal service and ceremonial contexts.

text: あ
translation: Oh.

text: 肝心の願いを考えておりませんでした
translation: I had not given any thought to what I actually wished for.

vocabulary.meaning: the crucial thing; the most important part

grammar: 〜ておりませんでした is the humble-past progressive negative of 〜ている (to have been doing / to have done); おります is the humble form of います.

text: これではいけませんね
translation: This simply will not do.

vocabulary.meaning: must not; will not do; that's no good

grammar: これではいけませんね is a set polite expression meaning 'this won't do / this is unacceptable,' softened by the sentence-final ね seeking light agreement.

text: 熟考の上また近いうちに訪れることにいたしましょう
translation: After due reflection, let us plan to visit again before long.

vocabulary.meaning: before long; in the near future

grammar: 〜ことにいたしましょう is a humble-volitional expression (いたす is humble for する); 〜ことにする means 'to decide to do,' and いたしましょう adds humility and a gentle proposal ('let us decide to…').

text: おや
translation: My, my.

text: こちらは何の施設でしょうか
translation: What sort of establishment might this be?
grammar: 〜でしょうか is a polite interrogative expressing wonder or inquiry ('I wonder if it is…'), more tentative and refined than plain ですか.

text: 中に険しいお顔立ちの御人がいらっしゃいますが
translation: There is a person inside with a rather stern countenance.

vocabulary.meaning: to be; to exist (honorific form of いる)

grammar: いらっしゃいます is the honorific (尊敬語) equivalent of います, used by Elizabeth to show respect even toward strangers she observes.

text: こちらに貼ってある顔写真は
translation: As for the photograph posted here…

vocabulary.meaning: photograph of a face; portrait photo

grammar: 〜てある expresses a resultant state caused by someone's deliberate action (the photo was posted and remains so), distinct from 〜ている which describes ongoing action.

text: 死ねいて敗、報奨金
translation: "Wanted — Reward"…
grammar: This segment appears to be Elizabeth reading aloud garbled/partial text from a wanted poster; the transcription is imperfect. null grammar note.

text: これは私の討伐依頼と同様のものと考えてよろしいのでしょうか
translation: Would I be correct in thinking this is something similar to the subjugation requests I receive?

vocabulary.meaning: good; acceptable (formal/polite form of いい)

grammar: 〜と考えてよろしいのでしょうか is a very polite inquiry ('may I think of it as…?'); よろしい is the formal/polite equivalent of いい, and でしょうか adds tentative politeness.

text: なるほど、池鳥でございますね
translation: I see — this is a police box, then.

vocabulary.meaning: I see; indeed; that makes sense
police box; koban (small neighborhood police station)
it is, isn't it (very polite copula + ね)

grammar: でございますね combines the highly formal copula でございます with sentence-final ね, used to lightly confirm a newly understood fact in a graceful, refined way.

text: 特診いたしました
translation: I have made a note of it.

vocabulary.meaning: likely a transcription of 特記 (特記いたしました) — 'I have made special note of it'

grammar: 〜いたしました is the humble-past form of する (いたす), used as Elizabeth records her observations with characteristic thoroughness and formality.

text: こちらの建物はまさかここはクラブ
translation: This building… surely this is not — a club?

vocabulary.meaning: surely not; don't tell me (expressing disbelief or surprise)

grammar: まさか introduces shocked disbelief ('surely not…'), and the sentence breaks off mid-clause, conveying Elizabeth's flustered excitement.

text: 内なるパトスのままに踊る
translation: Dancing freely according to one's inner pathos…

vocabulary.meaning: pathos; passion; deep emotion (from Greek πάθος)

grammar: 〜のままに means 'just as; in accordance with; at the mercy of' — ままに expresses acting without restraint according to something, here one's inner passion.

text: そんな日常では許されぬ欲求を解放する光と音の地下庭
translation: An underground garden of light and sound, liberating those desires that ordinary daily life would never permit.
grammar: 〜ぬ is the classical negative auxiliary (equivalent to 〜ない), giving 許されぬ ('not permitted') an archaic, literary tone consistent with Elizabeth's elevated register.

text: おっはっ 今はしまっているのです
translation: Oh! It appears to be closed right now.
grammar: 〜のです (contracted to 〜のです/んです) provides explanatory nuance — 'the fact is that it is closed' — here used to gently convey a discovered reality.

text: 残念でございます ぜひ私
translation: How unfortunate. I, for one, would very much like to...

vocabulary.meaning: polite copula (formal equivalent of です)

grammar: 〜でございます is the most formal tier of the copula, characteristic of Elizabeth's speech. The sentence trails off mid-thought, suggesting a cut-off line.

text: 思っておりました
translation: ...that is what I had been thinking.
grammar: 〜ておりました is the humble-language (謙譲語) past continuous of 〜ている; おる is the humble form of いる.

text: 幾分気が収まりました それにしても
translation: I have calmed down somewhat. Even so...

vocabulary.meaning: to calm down, to settle one's feelings

grammar: 気が収まる is an idiomatic expression meaning one's agitation or anger has subsided.

text: どの場所も大変興味深く目移りをしてしまいます よろしければあなたのおすすめを教えていただけません
translation: Every place is so deeply fascinating that I find my attention pulled in all directions. If you would be so kind, might you tell me your recommendation?

vocabulary.meaning: having one's eyes drawn from one thing to another; being unable to choose

grammar: 〜ていただけません is a highly polite request form: 〜ていただく (to humbly receive the favor of someone doing something) + potential negative used as a softened request.

text: カラオケ それはまさか私の秘密のレパート
translation: Karaoke? Could it be... the moment to unveil my secret reperto—

vocabulary.meaning: could it be, surely not (exclamation of surprise/realization)

grammar: The line is cut off mid-word (レパートリー truncated), a transcription artifact. まさか here is used not in its negative sense but as an exclamation of delighted recognition.

text: お披露目の時が訪れたようですね 下部音曲の本職の歌い手にワンボタンで挑戦できるという
translation: It seems the moment has come for my grand unveiling. To think that with a single button one can challenge a professional singer of popular music...
grammar: 〜という at the end functions as a quotative or explanatory particle, leaving the sentence open-ended in wonderment; it conveys 'the fact that...' or 'to think that...'

text: あの
translation: Ah...

text: あ失礼
translation: Oh, pardon me.

text: 少々お待ちいただけますか こちらにも噴水があったのですね
translation: Would you wait just a moment? Why, there is a fountain here as well.
grammar: 少々お待ちいただけますか is an extremely polite request: 少々 (a little) + お〜いただく (humble form of receiving a favor) + けますか (polite potential question).

text: さらにあちらにも噴水が
translation: And over there — another fountain!
grammar: The sentence ends with が, trailing off in excited astonishment — a common Japanese sentence-final particle usage expressing realization or mild exclamation.

text: なるほど この場所の噴水の主は三味一体ということなのですね
translation: I see... So the masters of the fountains in this place are a trinity — three in one.

vocabulary.meaning: I see, indeed, that makes sense
master, owner, spirit of a place
trinity (lit. three flavors, one body — a pun on 三位一体 'trinity')

grammar: 三味一体 is a playful pun: 三位一体 (さんみいったい, the Holy Trinity / three-in-one) rewritten with 味 (flavor), humorously applied to three fountains — characteristic of Elizabeth's quirky formal wordplay.

text: お待たせいたしました それでは参りましょう
translation: Thank you for waiting. Now then, shall we be on our way?

vocabulary.word: お待たせいたしました
vocabulary.reading: おまたせいたしました
vocabulary.meaning: sorry to have kept you waiting (formal apology)
let us go (humble volitional of 行く/来る)

grammar: お待たせいたしました uses いたす, the humble form of する, making this the most formal way to apologize for keeping someone waiting.

text: では参りましょう 我が主をたたえる歌
translation: Now then, let us proceed. A song in praise of my liege...

vocabulary.meaning: to praise, to extol, to glorify

grammar: 我が (わが) is an archaic/literary possessive pronoun meaning 'my' or 'our,' giving the phrase a solemn, classical feel befitting Elizabeth's speech.

text: ぜひご一緒に
translation: Please, join me.
grammar: ご一緒に uses the honorific prefix ご with 一緒に, elevating even 'together' to a polite register appropriate for Elizabeth.

text: おや?ご存じない?
translation: Oh my? You are not familiar with it?

vocabulary.meaning: oh my, why (expression of mild surprise)
to know (honorific form of 知っている)

grammar: ご存じ is the honorific (尊敬語) equivalent of 知っている/知っている; using it here shows Elizabeth respectfully referring to the protagonist's knowledge.

text: 本日は数々の貴重な体験をさせていただきました
translation: Today you have allowed me to partake in a number of precious experiences.
grammar: させていただきました is a humble expression meaning 'I was given the privilege of doing X'; it emphasizes gratitude and deference toward the protagonist.

text: 依頼の方は12分に達成でございます
translation: The request has been fulfilled to the fullest.

vocabulary.meaning: more than sufficiently, to the fullest (lit. twelve parts out of ten)

grammar: 十二分に (written here as 12分 in the source) is an idiomatic adverb meaning 'more than enough' — literally 'twelve-tenths' — emphasizing complete and thorough fulfillment.

text: よろしければまたいつかご一緒させていただきたく存じます
translation: Should it please you, I would very much like to accompany you again sometime.

vocabulary.meaning: if it pleases you, if you don't mind (formal conditional)
I think/feel (humble form of 思う)

grammar: 〜たく存じます is a highly formal construction: the 〜たく form (desire) of a verb + 存じます (humble 思う), expressing a wish with maximum deference.

text: お待ちしておりました
translation: I have been awaiting you.

vocabulary.word: お待ちしておりました
vocabulary.reading: おまちしておりました

grammar: お待ちしておりました combines the honorific お〜する (humble action toward the listener) with ておりました (humble continuous past), making this the most deferential way to say 'I was waiting for you.'

text: 行く手に歯向かい流れてくる階段
translation: Stairs that flow toward you against your advance...

vocabulary.meaning: one's path ahead, the way forward
to go against, to oppose, to face

grammar: Elizabeth describes an escalator in poetic, almost combative terms before naming it — a recurring character motif of dramatic over-description of mundane things.

text: これがエスカレーター
translation: So this is an escalator.
grammar: これが + noun is a classic structure for identification ('this is X'), here used as the culminating reveal after her poetic buildup in the previous line.

text: シンプルでありながら見た目以上の消耗を強いられる試練
translation: Simple in appearance, yet it is an ordeal that demands far greater exertion than it looks.

vocabulary.meaning: to force, to compel, to impose

grammar: 〜でありながら is a formal concessive ('while being X') equivalent to 〜だけど or 〜なのに, but more literary; 〜を強いられる is a passive form of 強いる, meaning 'to be compelled/subjected to.'

text: おや?良い子の皆様が危険とのことです
translation: Oh my? It seems that it is dangerous for well-behaved children.
grammar: 〜とのことです is a formal/indirect reportative expression meaning 'it is said that...' or 'apparently...', used here as Elizabeth reads a safety sign on the escalator.

text: 我々も注意して参りましょう
translation: We too shall proceed with caution.

vocabulary.meaning: to be careful, to pay attention

grammar: 参りましょう (humble volitional of 行く) is used again here, consistent with Elizabeth's formal register; 我々 is a formal plural pronoun rarely used in casual speech.

text: そしてこれは?
translation: And what might this be?

vocabulary.meaning: as for this, what is this

text: 足元にお気を付けください
translation: Please mind your step.

vocabulary.meaning: footing; one's feet; the ground underfoot

grammar: お〜ください is a polite honorific request form: お気を付けください = 'please take care (of your footing).'

text: この先に落とし穴がございます
translation: There is a pitfall ahead.

vocabulary.meaning: polite copula (extremely formal form of あります/です)

grammar: 〜でございます is Elizabeth's characteristic ultra-polite copula, the formal equivalent of 〜です/〜あります.

text: こちらでございます 柵で囲まれたこの中心にでございます
translation: It is right here — in the very center, enclosed by the fence.

vocabulary.meaning: surrounded; enclosed (passive past of 囲む)

grammar: 〜にでございます adds でございます to a locative phrase (〜に), emphasizing the location in a very formal register.

text: 目を引く看板で囲んだ上立ち入り禁止の文字ですが人は往々に禁じられたものほど触れてみたくなる
translation: The sign conspicuously proclaims 'No Entry,' yet people so often find themselves wanting to touch the very things they are forbidden to touch.

vocabulary.meaning: forbidden; prohibited (passive past of 禁じる)

grammar: 〜ほど〜(し)たくなる: 'the more something is X, the more one wants to Y' — a comparative degree construction expressing proportional desire.

text: 落とし穴は隠すものという常識を逆手に取った高度なトラップでございます
translation: It is a highly sophisticated trap that turns the conventional wisdom of 'pitfalls are meant to be hidden' completely on its head.

vocabulary.meaning: to turn something against itself; to use something to one's advantage in reverse

grammar: 〜を逆手に取る is a set phrase meaning 'to reverse-leverage X; to turn X on its head,' used here as a relative clause modifying トラップ.

text: 流れる足場に加えて心理トラップを組み合わせた落とし穴
translation: A pitfall that combines moving platforms with a psychological trap.
grammar: 〜に加えて means 'in addition to; on top of,' here linking 流れる足場 and 心理トラップ as combined elements.

text: 街の治安を守るとはかくも大変なことなのでございますね
translation: Protecting the peace of a city is truly an arduous undertaking, is it not?

vocabulary.meaning: so very; to such a degree (literary/formal)

grammar: かくも is a formal/literary adverb meaning 'to this extent; so very,' reinforcing Elizabeth's elevated register.

text: 胸を打たれております
translation: I am deeply moved.

vocabulary.meaning: to be deeply moved; to be touched to the heart

grammar: 〜ております is the formal progressive/resultant-state form (〜ている → 〜ております), indicating an ongoing emotional state in polite speech.

text: この街を愛する見知らぬどなたかの思いを噛みしめつつ
translation: While savoring the feelings of some unknown person who loves this city...

vocabulary.meaning: to savor; to chew over; to take to heart

grammar: 〜つつ is a literary/formal conjunctive meaning 'while doing X; as one does X,' indicating a simultaneous action or state.

text: それでは参りましょう
translation: Well then, shall we be on our way?

vocabulary.meaning: let us go (humble volitional of 行く/来る)

grammar: 参る is the humble (謙譲語) verb for 行く/来る; 〜ましょう makes it a polite volitional proposal: 'shall we go?'

text: これはこのかぐわしい香りはまさか
translation: This — this fragrant aroma — could it possibly be...?

vocabulary.meaning: surely not; could it be; don't tell me

grammar: まさか used in isolation (without a following clause) creates suspense — implying 'can this really be...?' with the rest left unsaid.

text: はあ驚いたわ
translation: Oh my, what a surprise!

vocabulary.meaning: to be surprised; to be astonished

text: この具の秘密匂いだけでわかるんか
translation: You can tell the secret ingredient just from the smell?
grammar: 〜だけで means 'just from; solely by,' emphasizing that smell alone was enough to identify the secret ingredient.

text: 姉ちゃん、だってにおもろい格好しとらんな
translation: Hey lady, you're not exactly dressed normal, are ya.

vocabulary.meaning: young lady; sis (casual address to a young woman)
interesting; funny; unusual (Osaka dialect for おもしろい)

grammar: 〜しとらんな is Kansai dialect: しとる = している (progressive), あらん/おらん = いない, combining to 'you're not dressed [normally], are you.'

text: ま、たこ焼き屋はたこ以外焼いたらあかんなんて法律あらへん
translation: Well, there's no law sayin' a takoyaki stand can only grill octopus.

vocabulary.meaning: there isn't; there's no (Osaka dialect for ない/ありません)

grammar: 〜なんて法律あらへん is Kansai dialect: なんて dismissively nominates the preceding clause ('there's no law that says...'), and あらへん is the negative of ある.

text: で、ちんとこう立ってや
translation: Now stand up nice and straight.

vocabulary.meaning: properly; smartly (dialectal/colloquial variant of ちゃんと)

grammar: 〜や is the Kansai imperative/request particle equivalent to standard Japanese 〜よ/ください: 立ってや = 'stand [properly], will you.'

text: ほっぺた落っこちてまうね
translation: Your cheeks are gonna fall right off!

vocabulary.meaning: to fall off; to drop (colloquial form of 落ちる)
to end up doing (Kansai dialect for しまう)

grammar: 〜てまう is Kansai dialect for 〜てしまう, indicating an action that happens completely or unintentionally: 'it'll end up falling off.'

text: ほっぺたが落ちる料理
translation: A dish so delicious your cheeks fall off...
grammar: This is Elizabeth literally parsing the idiom ほっぺたが落ちる ('so good your cheeks fall off') as a noun phrase, treating it as a descriptor for the food.

text: 現実には非常事態のような気もいたしますね
translation: In reality, it does feel rather like an emergency situation.

vocabulary.meaning: humble form of する (to do/feel)

grammar: 〜気もいたします is a humble, hedged expression: 気がする ('have a feeling that') made humble with いたす, softened further by も ('also; even').

text: ぜひとも体験してみたく存じます
translation: I would very much like to experience it.

vocabulary.meaning: by all means; most definitely (emphatic ぜひ)
humble equivalent of 思います (to think/feel)

grammar: 〜てみたく存じます combines the desiderative 〜たい (want to) in its conjunctive form with 存じます (humble 思う), yielding an extremely polite 'I would like to try.'

text: ですがあいにく持ち合わせはこちらだけ
translation: However, unfortunately all I have on me is this.

vocabulary.meaning: unfortunately; regrettably; as bad luck would have it
what one happens to have on hand; funds on one's person

grammar: 持ち合わせ is a noun meaning 'what one has on hand at the moment'; 〜はこちらだけ = 'only this [is all I have].'

text: これでどうにかお売りいただけるでしょうか
translation: Would you be so kind as to sell me some with this?

vocabulary.meaning: to humbly receive the favor of selling (to me)

grammar: お〜いただけるでしょうか is a maximally polite request form: honorific prefix お + verb stem + いただける (can I receive the favor of) + でしょうか (would it be possible).

text: 私実際にほっぺたを落としている方をお見かけしたことがございません
translation: In truth, I have never actually witnessed anyone whose cheeks have fallen off.

vocabulary.meaning: to happen to see; to catch sight of (humble/polite form of 見かける)
formal negative copula (polite form of ありません)

grammar: お見かけしたことがございません is a formal negative experiential: 〜たことがない ('have never done X') made polite with お〜する (humble) and ございません (formal negative).

text: おそらく市政のものには安々と手出しできない価格
translation: A price at which ordinary city dwellers could not easily reach out to buy.

vocabulary.meaning: residents of the city; those under city governance (slightly unusual phrasing for 'city folk/residents')
cannot easily touch/reach; out of one's reach

grammar: 〜には〜できない: 'for X, [doing Y] is not possible' — the には marks the subject from whose perspective the action is impossible.

text: は?よく見ましたらワンパック400円
translation: Hm? On closer inspection — one pack, 400 yen.

vocabulary.meaning: to look carefully; to take a closer look

grammar: は? at the start is an expression of mild surprise or recalibration, and よく見ましたら uses the たら conditional to mean 'upon looking more carefully' (a result clause with implicit discovery).

text: はっ
translation: Oh!

text: そ、それでは、2パックほどお願いいたします
translation: W-well then, I shall take two packs, if you please.
grammar: 〜ほど softens the quantity ('about two packs'); お願いいたします is the humble form of お願いします, elevating the request.

text: はい、ギニー、また来てや
translation: Here you go! Come again, yeah?
grammar: 〜てや is a Kansai-dialect variant of 〜てね, used for soft requests or farewells.

text: このプリプリした凶器に覆われた独特の食感は間違いなくあれ?
translation: This distinctive texture, encased in that plump, springy weapon — could it without doubt be... that?
grammar: 〜に覆われた is a passive relative clause modifying 食感: 'a texture covered/encased in ~'.

text: よもや食材として出会う時が来るとは驚きでございます
translation: To think there would come a day I would encounter it as an ingredient — how astonishing.
grammar: よもや〜とは expresses disbelief or amazement: 'to think that (something unexpected) would happen.'

text: いいえ特には何も
translation: No, nothing in particular.

text: ですが私食べてみたいものは他にもまだまだございます
translation: However, there are still so many other things I wish to try eating.

vocabulary.meaning: still many more; far from done
there are (polite form of あります)

grammar: 〜てみたい expresses the desire to try doing something: 食べてみたい = 'want to try eating.'

text: 考えてみればそれらを食事を得るまで
translation: When I think about it, until I have obtained all those meals...

vocabulary.meaning: when I think about it; come to think of it

grammar: 〜を得るまで means 'until obtaining ~'; the sentence trails off (…), building anticipation for the next line.

text: ほっぺたを失うわけにはまいりません
translation: I cannot afford to lose my cheeks.

vocabulary.meaning: cannot (humble negative of まいる; here ≈ いけません)

grammar: 〜わけにはまいりません is a humble, formal expression meaning 'cannot possibly do ~; it would not do to ~.'

text: この近辺にはまだまだ飲食の場がある様子
translation: It seems there are still many more places to eat and drink in this vicinity.

vocabulary.meaning: eating and drinking; food and drink

grammar: 〜様子 at the end of a noun phrase expresses inference from observation: 'it appears that ~; it seems ~.'

text: はしごというのをしてもよろしいでしょうか
translation: Would it be all right if we were to go bar-hopping, as it were?

vocabulary.meaning: bar-hopping; going from place to place (lit. 'ladder')

grammar: 〜というのをしてもよろしいでしょうか frames はしご as a concept she is quoting/borrowing: 'this thing called bar-hopping — may we do it?'

text: まずは漫画喫茶と呼ばれる場所にある ドリンクバーなる食材から参りましょう
translation: First, let us begin with the drink bar, that purveyor of ingredients, found in the establishment known as a manga café.

vocabulary.meaning: manga café (café with manga library and free drinks)
let us go; let us proceed (humble volitional)

grammar: 〜と呼ばれる場所 is a relative clause: 'a place called ~'; 参りましょう is the humble volitional, appropriate to Elizabeth's formal register.

text: 混合比によって無限の味が生み出せるというドリンクバー
translation: The drink bar, which they say can produce infinite flavors depending on the mixing ratio.
grammar: 〜によって indicates the means or cause: 'depending on / by means of the mixing ratio.'

text: 想像しただけで心持ちが高ぶるのを感じます
translation: Just imagining it, I can feel my heart beginning to flutter with excitement.

vocabulary.meaning: to become excited; to be stirred up

grammar: 〜だけで means 'just by doing ~; merely by ~': 想像しただけで = 'just by imagining it.'

text: なるほど
translation: I see.

vocabulary.meaning: I see; indeed; that makes sense

text: なんとまぁ
translation: My, my!

vocabulary.meaning: my goodness; well I never (exclamation of surprise)

text: これはまった
translation: Oh, this is...

text: これでこのあたりの料理はすべて食べ尽くしたようでございます
translation: It seems I have now eaten every dish this area has to offer.

vocabulary.meaning: to eat up entirely; to devour everything

grammar: 〜たようでございます expresses a polite inference: 'it appears that (I) have ~.'

text: あのどうかなさいましたか
translation: Um, is something the matter?

vocabulary.word: どうかなさいましたか
vocabulary.reading: どうかなさいましたか
vocabulary.meaning: is something the matter? are you all right? (very polite)

grammar: なさる is the honorific form of する; どうかなさいましたか is thus the very respectful way to ask 'did something happen to you?'

text: 思えば7食目あたりからあまりお箸が進んでおられないご様子でしたが
translation: Come to think of it, from around your seventh meal onward, it appeared your chopsticks were not advancing very much.

vocabulary.meaning: come to think of it; when I reflect on it

grammar: 〜ておられない is a respectful negative progressive (おられる = honorific いる): 'you were not [doing]'; directed at the protagonist with deference.

text: ともあれ本日は文字通りのおいしい体験をありがとうございました
translation: In any case, thank you for a truly — in the most literal sense — delicious experience today.

vocabulary.meaning: in any case; at any rate; be that as it may

grammar: ありがとうございました is the past-tense polite thanks, appropriate at the close of an outing; 文字通り humorously signals that Elizabeth means 'delicious' quite literally.

text: よろしければまたいつかご一緒させていただきたく存じます
translation: If you would not mind, I should very much like to accompany you again someday.

vocabulary.meaning: if it is all right with you; if you don't mind
I think/feel (humble form of 思う)

grammar: 〜させていただきたく存じます is an extremely deferential expression: 'I humbly wish to be permitted to ~,' combining causative-passive 〜させていただく with the desire form and humble 存じます.

text: お待ちしておりました
translation: I have been awaiting your arrival.

vocabulary.word: お待ちしておりました
vocabulary.reading: おまちしておりました

grammar: お〜しておりました combines the honorific prefix お〜する (humble action) with おる (humble form of いる) in the past progressive, conveying respectful anticipation.

text: ここが寺院によく似た施設 神社ですね
translation: So this is a shrine — a facility very similar to a temple.
grammar: 〜によく似た is an adjectival phrase meaning 'closely resembling ~'; Elizabeth compares the shrine to the temple with characteristic analytical curiosity.

text: 確かにシャドウなどとはまた違った
translation: Indeed, it has a somewhat different feel from Shadows and the like...

vocabulary.meaning: yet different; a different kind of

grammar: 〜などとはまた違った uses とは for contrast and また to add nuance: 'yet another kind of difference compared to things like ~.'

text: 神秘的で新たかな気配がいたします
translation: I sense a mystical and somehow novel presence here.

vocabulary.meaning: humble form of する (to do/sense)

grammar: 〜がいたします is a humble expression (謙譲語) equivalent to 〜がします (I sense / I feel), elevating the speaker's register.

text: ではこちらの様式にのったりましてまずは参拝をいたしましょう
translation: Then let us follow the customs here and first pay our respects at the shrine.

vocabulary.meaning: visiting and worshipping at a shrine or temple

grammar: 〜にのったりまして is a formal/archaic gerund form of 〜にのっとって (following/conforming to), characteristic of Elizabeth's elevated speech.

text: このくらいでしょうか
translation: About this much, I should think?

vocabulary.meaning: about this much, approximately this amount

grammar: 〜でしょうか is a polite question marker expressing uncertainty or seeking confirmation.

text: ひとまず納め終えました
translation: I have finished making my offering for now.

vocabulary.meaning: for the time being, for now
to finish offering/depositing (coins at a shrine)

grammar: 〜終えました is a compound verb form using 終える (to finish doing), indicating completion of the action.

text: これで日頃はこちらの住人でない私にも
translation: Come to think of it, even for someone like me who does not ordinarily reside here—

vocabulary.meaning: usually, normally, on a daily basis

grammar: This line is a sentence fragment ending in も, setting up a conditional or rhetorical follow-up (continued in idx 105).

text: ご利益が訪れますでしょうか
translation: —might divine blessings still find their way to me?

vocabulary.meaning: to visit, to come, to arrive

grammar: 〜ますでしょうか is an especially polite double-softened question form (〜ます + でしょうか), typical of Elizabeth's formal register.

text: 考えてみるとこの再生という仕組みは
translation: Come to think of it, this mechanism of regeneration—
grammar: 〜というのは / 〜という〜は is used to define or introduce a topic for elaboration; this line ends in a dash, leading into idx 107.

text: 噴水のそれとよく似ておりますね
translation: —bears a striking resemblance to that of a fountain, does it not?

vocabulary.meaning: to resemble, to be similar (classical/formal 〜ている)

grammar: そのそれ refers back to a previously mentioned noun's equivalent attribute ("its counterpart"); 〜ておりますね is the humble-continuous form of 〜ている with a seeking-agreement ね.

text: そこかしこに人々の幸福をかなえるスポットがある
translation: There are spots for fulfilling people's happiness scattered all about.

vocabulary.meaning: here and there, all around, everywhere

grammar: 〜がある at the end of the sentence is a plain-form existential construction, functioning as an embedded clause describing the land in idx 109.

text: 素敵な土地にお住まいなのですね
translation: You live in a truly wonderful place.

vocabulary.meaning: honorific form of 住まい (residence, where one lives)

grammar: お〜なのですね is an honorific-nominal construction (お住まいなのですね) expressing admiration while respectfully referencing the listener's situation.

text: あちらにたくさん結ばれている紙の帯は
translation: Those strips of paper tied in great numbers over there—

vocabulary.meaning: over there (polite/formal form of あそこ)
to be tied, to be bound

grammar: This is a dangling topic sentence (〜は) with the predicate left to the next utterance (idx 111–112), a natural speech pattern when pointing something out.

text: もしかし
translation: Could they perhaps be—

vocabulary.meaning: perhaps, could it be (truncated form of もしかして)

text: やはり私の期待通りおみくじでございます
translation: Just as I expected—they are omikuji fortune slips!

vocabulary.meaning: as expected, just as I thought
fortune slip drawn at a shrine or temple
formal/polite copula (very formal equivalent of です)

grammar: でございます is the most formal copula in Japanese, used by Elizabeth throughout to mark her elevated register.

text: 自らの運命をあえて紙切れ一枚に託し
translation: One dares to entrust one's very fate to a single slip of paper—

vocabulary.meaning: daringly, deliberately, going so far as to
scrap of paper, slip of paper
to entrust, to leave in the hands of

grammar: 〜に託し is a conjunctive form (te-form equivalent) of 託す, linking this clause to the next (idx 114).

text: そのリスク感を楽しむ遊戯と伺いましたが
translation: —and then savors the thrill of that risk. So I have been told.

vocabulary.meaning: sense of risk, thrill of risk
humble form of 聞く/聞いている (to hear, to be informed)

grammar: 〜と伺いましたが is a humble hearsay construction ("I have heard that..."), with が softening the statement or implying she is now verifying it.

text: なるほど運命について様々に書いてあるようですね
translation: I see—it does indeed appear to contain various writings about one's fate.

vocabulary.meaning: I see, indeed, that makes sense

grammar: 〜ようですね is an evidential expression ("it appears/seems that") based on visual observation, with ね seeking light agreement.

text: では一つ私も引いてみたいと存じます
translation: Well then, I too should like to try drawing one.

vocabulary.meaning: one (counter); also used to mean "just one" or "for once"
to draw (a lot, a fortune slip)
humble form of 思います (I think/would like)

grammar: 〜てみたいと存じます is a layered humble construction: 〜てみたい (want to try doing) + と存じます (I humbly think/feel), characteristic of Elizabeth's speech.

text: 全種類コンプリートするまで少々お待ちください
translation: Please wait just a moment while I complete the full set of every variety.

vocabulary.meaning: to complete, to collect all (from English "complete")

grammar: 〜するまでお待ちください is a polite request using お〜ください with a 〜まで temporal clause ("please wait until [I] do...").

text: あの先ほどから気になっておりましたが
translation: Excuse me—this has been on my mind for some time now, but—

vocabulary.meaning: to be curious about, to weigh on one's mind

grammar: 〜から気になっておりましたが uses the humble-continuous 〜ておりました (formal 〜ていた) with が softening into a lead-up to the question in idx 119.

text: あちらにあるものは何なのでしょうか
translation: Whatever might that thing over there be?

vocabulary.meaning: I wonder what it is (polite speculative question)

grammar: 〜なのでしょうか is a polite, softened question form expressing genuine curiosity or wonder rather than a direct question.

text: これは確かこちらが滑り台で
translation: Now, if I recall correctly, this one here is the slide—

vocabulary.meaning: if I recall correctly, I believe

grammar: 〜が is used mid-sentence as a connector, implying continuation into the next line (idx 121) while pausing to identify items one by one.

text: こちらがジャングルジム 誠の神前には形ばかりのおごそかさなど不要
translation: —and this one is the jungle gym. Before a truly divine presence, superficial solemnity is unnecessary.
grammar: 〜など不要 is a dismissive construction: など (and such things) + 不要 (unnecessary), used to emphatically dismiss something as irrelevant.

text: なんと寛大で本質に満ちた姿勢でしょう
translation: What a magnanimous and essence-filled attitude that is!
grammar: なんと〜でしょう is an exclamatory construction expressing admiration: "How [adjective] it is!"

text: でしたら早速
translation: In that case, right away—

vocabulary.meaning: in that case, if so (polite conditional)
at once, right away, without delay

text: これは楽しみを得るにはまず同じだけ登らねばならない
translation: To obtain the pleasure of descending, one must first climb the same distance—

vocabulary.meaning: must, have to (formal/literary equivalent of なければならない)

grammar: 〜ねばならない is a formal/literary variant of 〜なければならない (must do), fitting Elizabeth's archaic register; it expresses obligation or necessity.

text: 世の節理を無言にして教える奥深い遊具でございます
translation: It is a profoundly meaningful plaything that silently teaches the underlying principles of the world.
grammar: 〜にして: a formal/literary construction meaning 'while being ~' or 'by means of ~'; here 「無言にして」 means 'while remaining silent' / 'through silence'.

text: なかなかでございました
translation: That was quite something.

vocabulary.meaning: quite; rather; considerably (often implying unexpectedly good)

grammar: 〜でございました: past tense of the highly formal copula でございます, expressing polite past-tense judgment.

text: ではこちらのジャングルジムについても教えていただけますか
translation: In that case, would you be so kind as to tell me about this jungle gym as well?

vocabulary.word: 教えていただけますか
vocabulary.reading: おしえていただけますか

grammar: 〜ていただけますか: a polite request form ('could you please do ~?'), more deferential than 〜てください.

text: 出られません
translation: I cannot get out.

vocabulary.meaning: cannot get out; am unable to exit

grammar: 〜られません: potential-form negative (できません with movement verb 出る), indicating inability.

text: これはバランスが難しい
translation: This balance is quite difficult.

text: 本日は今までの外出にもまして楽しみました
translation: I enjoyed today's outing more than any of our previous ones.
grammar: 〜にもまして: a formal comparative expression meaning 'even more than ~'; 今までの外出にもまして = 'more than any outings up to now'.

text: 私実は近頃思うのですが
translation: Actually, I have been thinking lately…
grammar: 〜のですが: a softening sentence-final form that signals the speaker is about to say something or is leading into a point; leaves the thought trailing off.

text: 私がこちらの世界を楽しく感じるのは
translation: Is the reason I find this world enjoyable…
grammar: 〜のは: nominalizer + は, framing the preceding clause as the topic ('the reason/fact that I find ~ enjoyable is…'); the sentence is left incomplete, continuing in the next line.

text: ただ新鮮な刺激があるからなのでしょうか
translation: …simply because there are fresh stimulations to be had?
grammar: 〜からなのでしょうか: 'I wonder if it is because ~'; the combination of から (reason), の (nominalizer/explanatory), でしょうか (wondering/question) creates a reflective, self-questioning tone.

text: もしかすると私
translation: Or perhaps… it is I…
grammar: Sentence fragment trailing off with 私; Elizabeth is hesitating mid-thought, continued in the following lines.

text: あなたにお供する時間が楽しい
translation: …who finds the time spent accompanying you to be enjoyable.
grammar: お供する: humble compound verb (お + 供する) expressing that Elizabeth humbly accompanies the protagonist; the sentence ends without a copula, trailing into idx 136.

text: ということなのかもしれません
translation: …That may well be the case.
grammar: ということなのかもしれません: 'it may be that ~'; ということ nominalizes the preceding clause, and なのかもしれません adds polite conjecture.

text: ともあれまずは私どもの部屋に鉄棒など置いていただけないかと
translation: In any case, first I intend to petition that something like a horizontal bar be placed in our room.

vocabulary.meaning: in any case; be that as it may

grammar: 〜など: the particle など ('and such; or the like') softens the request, implying 'something like a horizontal bar'; a polite, non-demanding way to make a suggestion.

text: 主に掛け合う所存でございます
translation: …to negotiate with the Master.

vocabulary.meaning: master; lord (referring to Igor, the Velvet Room master)
to negotiate; to take the matter up with

grammar: 〜所存でございます: an extremely formal expression of one's firm intention, equivalent to 'I am resolved to ~'; 所存 is a formal/literary synonym for つもり.

text: よろしければまたいつかご一緒させていただきたく存じます
translation: If you are agreeable, I would very much like to accompany you again someday.

vocabulary.meaning: if it is agreeable to you; if you don't mind

vocabulary.word: ご一緒させていただく
vocabulary.reading: ごいっしょさせていただく
vocabulary.meaning: to have the honor of accompanying you (very humble)

grammar: 〜たく存じます: a very formal expression of desire/wish ('I humbly wish to ~'); たく is the desiderative stem of たい used in formal speech, and 存じます is the humble form of 思います.

text: ではそろそろお開きといたしましょう
translation: Well then, shall we soon bring things to a close?

vocabulary.meaning: close; end (of a gathering); breaking up

grammar: 〜といたしましょう: a formal volitional form ('let us ~'); いたす is the humble form of する, making this more polished than としましょう.

text: ですがその前に滑り台をワンモアお願いしたく
translation: However, before we do, I would like to request one more go on the slide.

vocabulary.meaning: I would like to request (formal, trailing)

grammar: 〜したく: the desiderative form したい truncated to したく, leaving the sentence grammatically incomplete — a very formal/literary way to trail off a request rather than state it directly.

text: せっかくですので2人乗りなどいかがですか
translation: Since we are here, how about we ride together — the two of us?

vocabulary.meaning: since we've gone to the trouble; while we're at it
riding together for two; tandem ride

grammar: 〜などいかがですか: 'how about ~ (or something like that)?'; など softens the suggestion and いかがですか is a polite way to propose something.

text: お待ちしておりました
translation: I have been awaiting you.

vocabulary.word: お待ちしておりました
vocabulary.reading: おまちしておりました

grammar: お〜しておりました: humble progressive past construction (お待ちする + おる past); more formal and deferential than 待っていました.

text: ここがあなたの学び屋
translation: So this is your place of learning—
grammar: 学び屋: a literary/archaic term for a school, built from 学び (learning) + 屋 (place/house); Elizabeth's elevated register favors this over the common 学校.

text: 月光館学園ですね
translation: —Gekkoukan High School, is it?

vocabulary.reading: げっこうかんがくえん
vocabulary.meaning: Gekkoukan High School (the school in Persona 3)

grammar: 〜ですね: sentence-final ね seeking confirmation or expressing gentle realization ('isn't it'; 'I see').

text: この明るく美しい場所がカルタロスに返じるとは
translation: To think that this bright and beautiful place transforms into Tartarus—

vocabulary.meaning: Tartarus (the Dark Hour dungeon in Persona 3)
to revert; to transform back into

grammar: 〜とは: an exclamatory/surprised construction ('to think that ~!'); expresses that the speaker finds the fact remarkable or hard to believe.

text: 私驚きを隠せません
translation: I cannot hide my astonishment.

vocabulary.meaning: cannot hide; am unable to conceal

grammar: 〜を隠せません: 'cannot conceal ~'; the potential-negative form of 隠す (to hide/conceal) expresses that one's emotion is beyond suppression.

text: これは困りました
translation: This is quite a predicament.

vocabulary.meaning: I am troubled; this is a problem (literally: became troubled)

grammar: 困りました as a fixed phrase: although past tense literally, これは困りました functions idiomatically as a present expression of being at a loss or troubled.

text: 皆様ご提携の服をお召しの様子
translation: It appears everyone is dressed in their matching uniforms.
grammar: 〜の様子: 'it appears that ~'; 様子 (appearance/state) used after a noun/clause to express an inference from observation, functioning like 〜ようだ in formal speech.

text: 私はいささか目立つようでございますね
translation: It would seem that I stand out rather conspicuously.

vocabulary.meaning: to stand out, to be conspicuous

grammar: 〜ようでございますね: polite conjecture with ございます; 'it appears/seems that ~' in formal register.

text: 何事もなければ良いのですね
translation: As long as nothing happens, that should be fine.
grammar: 何事もなければ: conditional 'if nothing (untoward) occurs'; も intensifies the negative scope.

text: では目立たないよう工夫を凝らすことにいたしましょう
translation: In that case, let us devise a way to avoid drawing attention.

vocabulary.meaning: let us do (humble volitional of する)

grammar: 〜ことにいたしましょう: humble-polite volitional expressing a decision to do something; 'let us go ahead and ~'.

text: こうして背中に隠れていればおおむね安心でございますね
translation: If I stay hidden behind your back like this, I should be mostly safe.

vocabulary.meaning: mostly, generally, for the most part

grammar: こうして〜ていれば: 'if I remain doing it this way'; conditional of the progressive て-form expressing a sustained state.

text: では校舎の中に向かいましょう
translation: Well then, let us head inside the school building.

vocabulary.meaning: to head toward, to make one's way to

grammar: 〜に向かいましょう: polite volitional with directional に; 'let us head to ~'.

text: これは驚きです。学校にもこのような販売施設に。
translation: How surprising. To think there is even a retail establishment like this inside a school.
grammar: Sentence-final に with falling intonation (〜に。) marks exclamatory emphasis or an incomplete thought trailing off in surprise.

text: 少々お待ちいただけますか。私、前々から気になっておりましたものは。
translation: Would you kindly wait just a moment? There is something I have been curious about for quite some time.

vocabulary.meaning: for a long time, for quite a while now
to be on one's mind, to be curious about

grammar: お待ちいただけますか: humble request form (お〜いただく) asking the listener to bestow the action of waiting upon her; very polite.

text: 失礼いたします。給食を売っていただきたいのですが。
translation: Excuse me. I would like you to sell me some school lunch, if you please.

vocabulary.meaning: excuse me (formal/humble apology before addressing someone)

grammar: 〜ていただきたいのですが: softened humble request; 'I humbly wish to receive the favor of ~' — the trailing が leaves it open-ended and polite.

text: うーん、はい?
translation: Umm… yes?

text: 学校で飲み口にすることができると言われる給食を味わってみたかったのですが
translation: I had wished to sample the school lunch that is said to be something one gets to enjoy at school.

vocabulary.meaning: taste, flavor (here used loosely for 'something to be savored/consumed'); lit. drinking/eating opening
to taste, to savor, to experience

grammar: 〜と言われる: relative clause meaning 'that is said to be ~'; attributively modifying 給食.

text: パンも昼食時の醍醐味と聞き及びました
translation: I have also heard that bread is one of the great delights of lunchtime.

vocabulary.meaning: the real pleasure/essence of something, the best part
to have heard, to have come to know by hearsay (formal)

grammar: 〜と聞き及びました: formal past tense of 聞き及ぶ; 'I have heard (from various sources) that ~'.

text: パンにいたしましょう
translation: I shall go with the bread.
grammar: 〜にいたしましょう: humble decision form; 'I shall make it ~' / 'I'll have the ~'.

text: 念願かなったところで次へと参りましょう
translation: Now that our long-held wish has been fulfilled, let us move on to the next.

vocabulary.meaning: to be granted, to come true, to be fulfilled

grammar: 念願かなったところで: 'now that the wish has been granted'; ところで here marks 'at the point where ~ has just occurred', providing a transition.

text: これからの順路ですがまずはあなたの教室を覗いてみたく存じます
translation: As for our route from here — first, I would very much like to peek into your classroom.

vocabulary.meaning: to peek into, to look in on
I think/feel (humble form of 思う)

grammar: 〜てみたく存じます: humble form of 〜てみたい; 'I humbly wish to try ~ing'; 存じます elevates the politeness level further.

text: ここが教室
translation: So this is the classroom.
grammar: Short nominal sentence (ここが教室): topic + noun predicate, omitting the copula for a clipped, observational tone.

text: わずかこれだけの広さの中に机の数だけの人数が強制するとは
translation: To think that a number of people equal to the number of desks are forced into a space this small…
grammar: 〜とは: exclamatory とは expressing surprise or disbelief; 'to think that ~!' The sentence trails off, mimicking Elizabeth's amazement.

text: いえ違いますね
translation: No, that is not it.

text: 他者と調和する力を育むため
translation: In order to cultivate the ability to live in harmony with others…

vocabulary.meaning: to nurture, to foster, to cultivate

grammar: 〜ため: purpose marker; 'for the sake of / in order to ~'; the sentence is deliberately left incomplete, as Elizabeth revises her thought mid-speech.

text: わざとこのように奥深い配慮を感じます
translation: I sense an intentionally profound consideration at work here.
grammar: 〜を感じます: 'I sense/feel ~'; direct object + 感じる in polite present form.

text: この監視用の物見台が俗に申します
translation: This observation platform for supervision is what is commonly called…

vocabulary.meaning: is commonly called, is colloquially known as (humble)

grammar: 俗に申します: humble form of 俗に言う; 'is commonly/colloquially said to be ~'; sentence breaks off, indicating she is about to name something.

text: 教団でございますね
translation: The teacher's podium, is it not.
grammar: 〜でございますね: polite copula + ね seeking light confirmation; note that 教団 (religious sect) in the source is almost certainly a mishearing/OCR error for 教壇 (teacher's podium), which fits the context.

text: 確かに
translation: Indeed.

text: ここに立つと思わず教鞭を取りたい誘惑に駆られます
translation: Standing up here, I find myself irresistibly tempted to take up the teacher's pointer.

vocabulary.meaning: to take up the teaching rod, to teach (set phrase)
to be driven by, to be seized with (an urge)

grammar: 思わず〜に駆られます: 'involuntarily/unwittingly seized by ~'; 思わず signals an impulse one cannot help; 〜に駆られる expresses being driven by a feeling.

text: 第1問
translation: Question number one.

text: ダイエットフードとダイエットフード貝
translation: Diet food and… diet food shellfish?
grammar: Garbled/fragmentary line; 貝 (shellfish) appended to the second instance likely represents a mishearing or text error. Best-effort rendering preserves both elements.

text: 美味しいのはどちらでしょう
translation: Which one do you suppose is the more delicious?
grammar: 〜のはどちらでしょう: nominalizer の turns the preceding clause into a noun phrase; でしょう is a soft speculative question, more polite than ですか.

text: 正解でございます
translation: That is the correct answer.

vocabulary.meaning: formal/polite copula (ございます-form of です)

grammar: でございます is the most formal register of the copula です, characteristic of Elizabeth's elevated speech.

text: 見事正解を選ばれたあなたには景品のダイエットフード貝を申請いたします
translation: For correctly selecting the right answer, I shall put in a request for the prize — a diet food shell — on your behalf.

vocabulary.meaning: humble form of します (to do)

grammar: 〜を申請いたします: いたします is the humble (謙譲語) form of する, raising the politeness of the verb 申請する.

text: 授業とはおおむねこのような形でよろしいのでしょうか
translation: Is a class generally conducted in this sort of manner?
grammar: 〜でよろしいのでしょうか: a very polite way to confirm or seek agreement, literally 'would it be all right if it were ~?'

text: そろそろ後期の目線が気になってまいりましたので他へ移動しましょう
translation: I have begun to feel the gaze of those in the back rows upon us, so let us move somewhere else.

vocabulary.meaning: back rows / rear section (here: 後席 likely intended, but read as 後期: latter period — context suggests those seated behind)

grammar: 〜が気になってまいりました: まいりました is the humble form of 来ました; 〜てまいる expresses a gradual onset ('has come to become') in polite speech.

text: 人間型の石膏像が中身が出てこないよう石膏で固めているのでしょうか
translation: I wonder — are human-shaped plaster statues encased in plaster so that what is inside does not come out?

vocabulary.meaning: to harden, to encase, to set firm

grammar: 〜ないよう〜でしょうか: ないよう (so that ~ does not) modifies the purpose of the action; でしょうか adds a speculative, wondering tone.

text: 少々窮屈に思いますが
translation: It seems it would feel rather cramped, though.
grammar: 〜に思いますが: 〜に思う expresses a subjective impression; the trailing が softens the statement, leaving it open-ended.

text: ピアノでしたら多少は覚えがございます
translation: As for the piano, I do have some recollection of it.

vocabulary.meaning: formal polite form of あります

grammar: 覚えがございます: a formal expression meaning 'I have some knowledge/memory of it'; ございます elevates ある to its most polite level.

text: ベルベットの歌
translation: The Velvet Song.

text: ご存知ですね
translation: You know it, don't you.

vocabulary.meaning: honorific form of 知っている (to know)

grammar: ご存知ですね: ご存知 is a respectful expression (sonkeigo) meaning 'you know'; ですね seeks gentle confirmation.

text: ベルベルベルベルベルベット
translation: Vel-vel-vel-vel-vel-vet~

vocabulary.meaning: velvet — Elizabeth's playful repetition of the word

text: 我が主長い花
translation: My lord, the long flower~
grammar: 我が is a classical/literary first-person possessive, reinforcing Elizabeth's archaic register.

text: はいご一緒に
translation: Now, sing along with me!
grammar: はい is used here as an encouraging cue ('okay, ready!'); ご一緒に is the polite/honorific form of 一緒に.

text: 本日は体験入学をさせていただき より一層世界観が広がりました
translation: Today, having had the privilege of a trial enrollment, my sense of the world has broadened all the more.
grammar: 〜させていただき: humble form expressing that she was graciously permitted to do something; connects two clauses, with the result stated after.

text: よろしければまたいつかご一緒させていただきたく存じます
translation: If it would suit you, I should very much like to accompany you again sometime.

vocabulary.meaning: humble form of 思います (to think, to feel)

grammar: 〜させていただきたく存じます: a highly formal expression of desire; たく is the conjunctive form of たい; 存じます is humble 思います.

text: 実は私 なぜことさらにここを訪れたいと思ったのか
translation: The truth is, I myself am not sure why I felt such a particular desire to come here.
grammar: なぜ〜のか: embedded question structure; のか nominalizes the clause, making 'why I wanted to...' the subject of the sentence.

text: 自分でもよくわからない ですがあなたに身を寄せて歩いている間
translation: I don't quite understand it myself. Yet while walking close by your side...

vocabulary.meaning: to draw close to, to lean toward someone

grammar: 〜ている間: expresses duration ('while [action] is ongoing'); here it sets up a contrast with her uncertainty about why she came.

text: 私 なんというか
translation: I feel... how shall I put it...

vocabulary.meaning: how shall I put it, what can I say (filler/hedge)

grammar: なんというか is a conversational filler used to buy time or soften what follows; Elizabeth's use of it is charmingly out of place given her usual precision.

text: とても充実しておりましたもしかすると私はあなたのことをよく知りたいのかもしれません
translation: I felt very fulfilled. Perhaps I wish to know you better.

vocabulary.meaning: to know well, to come to understand deeply

grammar: 〜かもしれません (here: かもしれません implied via かもしれません context): expresses possibility/conjecture; もしかすると reinforces the tentativeness.

text: 一体どうしてっ ともあれこの原因を究明するまでは退屈せずに済みそうか
translation: Why on earth...! Well, in any case, it seems I shall not be bored until I uncover the cause.

vocabulary.meaning: on earth, in the world (emphatic interrogative)
in any case, be that as it may
investigation, getting to the bottom of

grammar: 〜せずに済みそう: 〜ずに済む means 'to manage without doing ~'; 済みそう adds conjecture ('it seems I can get by without'); here: 'it seems I won't have to be bored.'

text: では戻るといたしましょう お疲れ様でございました
translation: Well then, let us return. You have worked hard today — thank you for your efforts.

vocabulary.meaning: humble volitional form of する (let us do)
thank you for your hard work (set phrase)

grammar: 〜といたしましょう: combines と (quotation/content marker) with いたしましょう (humble volitional); a polished way to propose an action.

text: ふふっ
translation: Heh heh.

text: お待ちしておりました
translation: I have been awaiting you.

vocabulary.word: お待ちしておりました
vocabulary.reading: おまちしておりました

grammar: お〜しておりました: the combination of honorific prefix お, humble verb する, and おります (humble いる) creates the most formal register of 'to wait.'

text: ここがあなたの住んでいる学生寮ですね
translation: So this is the student dormitory where you live.
grammar: 〜ていている is a relative clause modifying 学生寮; ですね at the end confirms what she is observing, with a gentle seeking of agreement.

text: ここがあなたの部屋
translation: So this is your room.
grammar: Sentence ends without a copula — the abrupt trailing-off (ここがあなたの部屋) conveys Elizabeth's wide-eyed wonder, letting the moment speak for itself.

text: 見慣れないものに囲まれておりますね
translation: We are surrounded by things I am unaccustomed to seeing.
grammar: 〜ておりますね: 〜ている in humble register (おる), with the sentence-final ね inviting shared acknowledgment.

text: ところであなたの部屋に出かけたいという私の依頼についてですが
translation: By the way, regarding my request to go out to your room—
grammar: 〜についてですが: 「〜について」 (concerning/regarding) + ですが softens and sets up a topic, leaving the sentence deliberately trailing.

text: そのご不審に思われませんでしたか
translation: Did that not strike you as suspicious?
grammar: 〜に思われませんでしたか: the passive/honorific 〜れる attached to 思う plus negative past question, politely asking whether the listener felt a certain way.

text: そうでしたか
translation: Is that so.

vocabulary.meaning: Is that so; I see (mild acknowledgment)

text: 実は私降り行ってお話ししたいことが
translation: The truth is, I have something I have been meaning to come and speak with you about.

vocabulary.meaning: to go out of one's way; to take the trouble to come (archaic/formal)

grammar: 降り行って (折り入って in standard orthography): a formal expression meaning 'going to the trouble of coming specifically,' signaling an important or heartfelt matter ahead.

text: こちらの世界を探望して私は多くのものに触れました
translation: In exploring this world, I have encountered a great many things.

vocabulary.meaning: to come into contact with; to experience; to touch

grammar: 〜して私は〜に触れました: the te-form links clauses (exploring → coming into contact), giving a sequential and cumulative feel.

text: 何もかもが忘れられない思い出
translation: Each and every thing is an unforgettable memory—

vocabulary.meaning: each and every thing; everything without exception

grammar: Nominal sentence (no verb): the phrase ends as a noun, building into the metaphor of the next line.

text: きらめく光珠のようでございます
translation: They are like glittering jewels of light.
grammar: 〜ようでございます: でございます is the highly polite copula (ございます register); 〜よう expresses likeness or appearance.

text: にぎわう街並みを歩いたり
translation: We walked through the lively city streets,

vocabulary.meaning: to be bustling; to be lively
townscape; row of shops and buildings

grammar: 〜たり: the 〜たり〜たりする construction (continued in the next line) lists actions as representative examples from a series.

text: 食を楽しんだり神社で無邪気に過ごして
translation: enjoyed food, spent carefree time at a shrine,
grammar: Continuation of 〜たり list from idx 208; the て-form 過ごして flows into the next clause.

text: あなたの学校にも行って
translation: and also visited your school—

text: そして私気がついたのでございます
translation: And then, I realized something.

vocabulary.meaning: to notice; to realize; to become aware

grammar: 〜のでございます: の nominalizes and adds explanatory nuance; ございます keeps the high-register tone, here marking a significant personal revelation.

text: 私は無意識に依頼の回を追うごとに
translation: Without realizing it, with each request,
grammar: 〜ごとに: attached to nouns or counters, means 'each time; with every instance of'—here 回を追う (as outings accumulate) + ごとに.

text: よりあなたに近しい場所を指定しておりました
translation: I had been designating places that brought me closer and closer to you.
grammar: 〜ておりました: humble continuous past (おる + ました), indicating an ongoing unconscious action she is now reflecting upon.

text: ですから本日はこちらの世界で最も深くあなたを知り得る場所
translation: And so today I wished to go to the place in this world where one can know you most deeply—

vocabulary.meaning: to be able to know; to come to know (potential form)

grammar: 〜得る (える/うる): potential auxiliary attached to verb stem, meaning 'able to'; used in more formal/literary contexts than the plain potential 〜られる.

text: あなたの部屋に出かけたいと依頼させていただいた次第でございます
translation: which is why I took the liberty of requesting to go to your room.

vocabulary.meaning: the reason/circumstances; this is why (formal closing expression)
to humbly do (highly polite request/action form)

grammar: 〜させていただいた次第でございます: a very formal closing formula; 次第 explains the reason/conclusion and でございます maintains the elevated register.

text: 失礼いたします
translation: Pardon me.

vocabulary.meaning: excuse me; pardon me (formal, used when entering a space)

text: 覚えておいてでしょうか
translation: Do you recall?
grammar: 覚えておいてでしょうか: likely 覚えておいででしょうか (honorific continuous 〜ていらっしゃる → 〜ておいで), a polite inquiry asking if the listener is still holding something in memory.

text: 以前学校を案内していただいたり
translation: When you showed me around the school before,
grammar: 〜していただいたり: 〜ていただく (to have someone do something for one, humble) + たり lists it as one of a set of recalled events.

text: あなたに触れた私が充実を感じると申し上げたこと
translation: and that I told you I felt fulfilled whenever I was close to you.

vocabulary.meaning: to be near; to come in contact with; to touch
fulfillment; a sense of richness or completeness

grammar: 〜と申し上げたこと: the quotation particle と + 申し上げる (humble 'to say') + こと nominalizes the whole clause, making it the object of 覚えておいででしょうか from idx 217–218.

text: 私にとってああいった心境の変化は初めてのことでございました
translation: For me, such a change of heart was an entirely new experience.

vocabulary.meaning: that kind of; such (referring to something previously mentioned)
change of heart; shift in one's emotional state

grammar: 〜でございました: past tense of the polite copula でございます, marking this as a reflection on a past (unprecedented) inner experience.

text: どうして私は充実を感じたのか
translation: Why had I felt that sense of fulfillment?
grammar: Rhetorical question in plain form (〜のか implied): Elizabeth voices aloud the inner question she had been wrestling with, drawing the listener in.

text: 私こちらを訪れてようやくその疑問の答えにたどり着きました
translation: By coming here, I have finally arrived at the answer to that question.

vocabulary.meaning: to finally reach; to arrive at after a journey

grammar: 〜てようやく〜にたどり着く: the te-form sets a prerequisite condition (visiting here), after which ようやく emphasizes the long-sought nature of the arrival.

text: 答えは実感だと存じます
translation: I believe the answer is presence — a genuine sense of being real.

vocabulary.meaning: a real, lived feeling; genuine sense of something being real

grammar: 〜と存じます: 存じる is the humble form of 思う/知る; 〜と存じます is a formal, deferential way of stating one's conclusion or belief.

text: ベルベットルームの住人である者が心待ちにするのは客人
translation: What a resident of the Velvet Room awaits is a guest—

vocabulary.meaning: to look forward to; to eagerly await

grammar: 〜である者が〜するのは: 者 (one who is) introduces a category of person; のは then topicalizes what that person does, setting up a contrast or revelation to follow.

text: その訪れだけが外界との接点であり
translation: Those visits alone are the point of contact with the outside world,
grammar: 〜であり is a conjunctive form of だ/である, linking clauses formally: 'is … and.'

text: 私どもに意義を与える
translation: and grants meaning to those of us here.
grammar: 私ども is the humble plural of 私, characteristic of Elizabeth's very formal register.

text: こうしてあなたに触れることで私はそれを得るのでございます
translation: It is through touching your world like this that I obtain it.

vocabulary.meaning: to touch; to come into contact with
formal copula (polite equivalent of です)

grammar: 〜ことで expresses means or cause: 'by doing ~,' 'through doing ~.'

text: いっそありていに申し上げます
translation: Allow me to speak plainly.

vocabulary.meaning: rather; frankly; just go ahead and

grammar: 申し上げます is the humble-polite form of 言う; ありていに申し上げる is a set phrase meaning 'to speak frankly.'

text: 私世間知らずゆえに色々ととんきょなこともあったかとは存じますが
translation: I know I must have done some rather odd things, being so unfamiliar with the world,

vocabulary.meaning: inexperienced in the ways of the world; naïve

grammar: 〜かとは存じますが softens the admission: 'I believe there may have been … but' — a humble, hedged concession.

text: さすがに私でも殿方の資質に上がり込む意味くらいは存じております
translation: Even I know what it means to step into a gentleman's quarters.

vocabulary.meaning: even so; as one would expect
here: quarters, premises (lit. 'quality/nature' — likely 私室/quarters by context)

grammar: 〜くらいは存じております: 'at least I do know ~' — くらい minimizes the claim while は adds contrast/emphasis.

text: もしあなたさえよろしければお手引きをいただきたいのです
translation: If it would be agreeable to you, I would very much like your guidance.

vocabulary.meaning: if it is acceptable to you

grammar: もし〜さえよろしければ: 'if only you are willing' — さえ restricts the condition to just that one factor.

text: ありがとうございます
translation: Thank you very much.

vocabulary.word: ありがとうございます
vocabulary.reading: ありがとうございます

text: ございます
translation: …Yes.

vocabulary.meaning: formal existential/copula (polite form of ある/です)

grammar: A lone ございます functions as an affirmative acknowledgment — formal and understated.

text: 初めてこちらの世界に来た頃とは
translation: Compared to when I first came to this world…
grammar: 〜とは sets up a contrast with what follows; here it implies 'unlike back then.'

text: まるで別人になった自分がいる気がいたします
translation: I feel as though I have become an entirely different person.

vocabulary.meaning: to do (humble); here: いたします as humble form of します

grammar: まるで〜気がいたします: 'I have the feeling that, as if ~' — まるで reinforces the simile of complete transformation.

text: これ以上こちらに留まっては
translation: If I were to remain here any longer,

vocabulary.meaning: any more than this; any further

grammar: 〜ては sets up a negative consequence: 'if I were to do ~, [something bad would follow].'

text: 己の本来の役割を忘れてしまいそう
translation: I feel I might forget my true purpose.
grammar: 〜そう (〜しそう) expresses that something seems likely to happen: 'it seems as though I might forget.'

text: ですがそれはあなたにとっても不利益
translation: And that would not be in your best interests, either.
grammar: The sentence is nominalized — ですが connects to the prior line, and にとっても adds 'for you as well.'

text: ですからこちらの世界を巡り歩くのは
translation: And so, wandering this world of yours—

vocabulary.meaning: to go around; to wander through

text: これを最後にさせていただきたいと存じます
translation: —I would like to make this my last time.

vocabulary.meaning: would like to humbly do ~ (causative + いただく)

grammar: 〜させていただきたいと存じます is a deeply humble expression: 'I humbly wish to be permitted to do ~.'

text: 私の好奇心に最後までお付き合いいただき
translation: For accompanying my curiosity to the very end,
grammar: お〜いただき is the honorific-humble form of もらう: 'for having received the favor of your company.'

text: 本当にありがとうございました
translation: I truly thank you from the bottom of my heart.

vocabulary.word: ありがとうございました
vocabulary.reading: ありがとうございました
vocabulary.meaning: thank you very much (past, for something now concluded)

grammar: The past form ございました (vs. ございます) marks that the shared experience is now complete — a farewell.

text: 本当に
translation: Truly.

text: それでは名残惜しいですが参りましょう
translation: Well then — it is difficult to part, but let us be on our way.

vocabulary.meaning: reluctant to part; loath to say goodbye
let us go (humble volitional of 行く/来る)

grammar: 参りましょう is the humble-volitional of 参る (行く/来る), inviting departure with formal grace.
